answer: Require every identity to build a sequential work history: each task is issued only after the previous one is peer-graded, and its content depends on that grade, like light through a prism splitting one beam into a single ordered spectrum. A Sybil cannot shortcut the chain: a fresh identity must redo the whole history from zero, one graded step at a time, while the relic of past work stays bound to the original identity. Ten fake identities cost ten full sequential histories, and no ferrous-fast parallel farm can compress a chain whose next link needs the previous grade.
